title: Deployments, rollouts and rollbacks
summary: Ship a new version with no downtime, watch it, and undo it.

steps.title: Deployment owns ReplicaSets
body: A **Deployment** manages ReplicaSets; ReplicaSets manage pods.

Change anything in the pod **template** (image, env, resources) and the Deployment creates a **new** ReplicaSet, then scales the new one up and the old one down. Changing only `replicas` scales the current ReplicaSet and does not start a rollout.
kubectl rollout status deploy/shop-api      waits until done (CI uses this)
kubectl rollout undo deploy/shop-api        back to the previous ReplicaSet
Old ReplicaSets are kept at 0 replicas (`revisionHistoryLimit`, default 10) precisely so `undo` is instant.

steps.prompt: Which change to a Deployment starts a new rollout (a new ReplicaSet)?
options: Changing an environment variable in the container spec
Adding a label to the Deployment's own metadata
steps.explain: Only changes under `spec.template` produce a new pod-template-hash and therefore a new ReplicaSet.

steps.title: maxSurge and maxUnavailable
body: The `RollingUpdate` strategy has two knobs, relative to `replicas`:
- **maxSurge**: how many pods *above* `replicas` may exist during the update (default 25%, rounded **up**).
- **maxUnavailable**: how many *below* `replicas` may be unready (default 25%, rounded **down**).
1     4    1     5     <- surge one new pod, wait until it is Ready

`maxUnavailable: 0` keeps full capacity but needs spare room in the cluster for the surge pod. The other strategy, `Recreate`, kills all old pods first: downtime, but never two versions at once (needed when versions cannot share a database schema).

If new pods never become Ready, the rollout **stalls**: old pods keep serving, and `rollout status` eventually reports `progress deadline exceeded`. That safety net only works if you have a readiness probe (module 5).

steps.prompt: `replicas: 10`, `maxSurge: 25%`, `maxUnavailable: 25%`. What are the most pods that can exist, and the fewest that must be available, during the rollout?
options: 13 pods at most, 8 available at least
steps.explain: Surge rounds up: 25% of 10 = 2.5 → 3, so 13. Unavailable rounds down: 2.5 → 2, so at least 8 available.
hints: Surge rounds up, unavailable rounds down.

steps.prompt: Version 1.5 is broken in production and you have decided to roll back. Order the commands: look at the rollout and its revisions before you act, roll back, wait until the rollback is complete, and only then read the logs of the restored pods.
steps.explain: Confirm the state, see which revisions exist, undo, wait for it to finish, then check the logs. Afterwards fix the manifest in Git too, or the next apply reintroduces 1.5.

steps.prompt: Rounding the percentages. What does this print?

You changed only the image tag and applied. Fill in the line `kubectl get rs` shows for the **old** ReplicaSet once the rollout is complete: type the DESIRED, CURRENT and READY numbers separated by single spaces.
steps.explain: The old ReplicaSet is kept, scaled to zero, so `kubectl rollout undo` can scale it straight back up.

steps.title: Rescue a stuck rollout
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`). A release of `api` went out ten minutes ago and has not finished: `kubectl rollout status deploy/api`
never returns (Ctrl+C), and `kubectl get pods` shows why.
1. Find out what is wrong with the new pods.
2. Roll the Deployment **back** to the previous revision, and wait until it is complete again with 4 ready pods.
3. Write the revision number that `api` is at **after** the rollback into `~/answers/revision.txt`

checks.name: api is back to the working image, fully rolled out
checks.fail: `api` should run `traefik/whoami:v1.11` again with 4 updated, 4 ready pods. `kubectl rollout undo deploy/api`.

checks.name: no broken pods are left
checks.cmd: kubectl get pods -l app=api -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}' | sort -u
checks.fail: Some `api` pods still run the broken image.

checks.name: revision.txt is the current revision
checks.fail: Not the current revision. A rollback does not go back to revision 1: it creates a **new** revision from the old template.

hints: `kubectl get pods` shows `ImagePullBackOff`; `kubectl describe pod NAME` says which image could not be pulled.
`kubectl rollout history deploy/api` lists the revisions with their change-cause; `kubectl rollout undo deploy/api` returns to the previous one.
`kubectl rollout status deploy/api`, then read the revision with `kubectl rollout history deploy/api` (the last line).
solution: kubectl describe pods -l app=api | grep -m1 -i 'failed to pull'
steps.explain: A rolling update never takes down more than `maxUnavailable` pods, so the broken release stalled with most of the old pods still serving: the safety net working. `rollout undo` scales the previous ReplicaSet back up and records it as a **new** revision (3, not 1), which is why history shows change-causes. With a `progressDeadlineSeconds` the Deployment would also report `ProgressDeadlineExceeded`, which CI can watch with `kubectl rollout status --timeout`.
